reviewed_pair_and_rank_proof:
# GF16 output pairs and eight-gate high-degree rank budget

This is a bounded mathematical review and independent replay, not a new SAT
search or an eight-AND exclusion. Field arithmetic uses F16 = F2[t]/(t^4+t+1).
All affine corrections, including constants, are free. Gate counts count binary
ANDs; XORs are free.

## Pair classes: five plus thirty, not six versus seven

The nondegenerate trace pairing identifies an output covector with a unique
field element a by lambda_a(z)=Tr(a z). A 2D output space is therefore a plane
L=<a,b>. Scaling one input scales L by a nonzero field element; applying the
same Frobenius to both inputs induces an inverse Frobenius on the trace
coefficients. Inverses generate the same cyclic group, so this distinction does
not change the orbit classification.

After scaling a to 1, write r=b/a, r not 0 or 1. Changing the ordered basis of
L replaces r by one of r, 1/r, 1+r, 1/(1+r), r/(1+r), (1+r)/r. These six maps
are the GL(2,2) action. The two roots of r^2+r+1 form the special ratio class;
the other twelve ratios form two classes of size six, exchanged by squaring.
The audit checks these fourteen ratios directly, independently of the parent's
35-plane enumeration.

The special planes are the five multiplicative cosets a F4 in F16. Their
scaling stabilizer has size three. A generic plane has trivial scaling
stabilizer: a nonidentity stabilizing multiplier would generate a field that
acts on the binary 2D plane, so it must generate F4, forcing the plane to be
a F4. There are consequently two generic scaling orbits of fifteen, merged
by Frobenius. Thus the complete semilinear orbit sizes are five and thirty.

This classification is structural, not a complexity gap. The parent produced
six-AND bilinear circuits for all 35 planes from its known nine-AND multiplier
and semilinear input changes. This audit independently replays every circuit
on all 256 input assignments, with two checked output bits per assignment.
The parent source is hash-pinned in report.json. No parent synthesis module
is imported by audit.py.

## Elementary quadratic lower bound: six

For any nonzero a, the bilinear matrix of Tr(a xy) is nonsingular of rank four:
for x nonzero, choose y so that Tr(a xy)=1. The alternating polar matrix is
therefore nonsingular of rank eight. This is also checked for all fifteen
nonzero output masks by the independent arithmetic implementation.

For k parallel affine-input ANDs, every nonzero target combination has a
decoder word of weight at least four, since one product has polar rank at
most two. For two outputs there are three nonzero decoder words. Their weight
sum is at least twelve and at most 2k: each nonzero decoder column contributes
exactly two. Therefore k>=6. At equality, all three weights are four, every
column is nonzero, and each column type 10, 01, 11 occurs exactly twice.

The all-quadratic-gate version follows either from the level-one circuit
definition used in the literature or from the separately retained Boolean
quadratic-flattening lemma for eight inputs. No assertion that an arbitrary
nonlinear circuit's decoder has this weight bound is being made.

The verified upper circuits and this lower bound establish quadratic and
bilinear pair complexity exactly six for both orbit classes.

## Published two-output theorem and its limits

Mirwald and Schnorr, Theoretical Computer Science 102 (1992), 307–328,
DOI 10.1016/0304-3975(92)90235-8, are explicitly credited with equality of
unrestricted and level-one multiplicative complexity for one or two quadratic
Boolean outputs in Boyar–Find (2018), page 8, and Bilgin et al. (2020),
section 2.2 / printed page 148. The original publisher's abstract was available,
but its full proof was not inspected in this run. This is an attributed theorem
dependency, not a theorem reproved or formally certified here.

Invoking that theorem transfers the independent quadratic lower bound to
unrestricted Boolean AND/XOR circuits. Together with the explicit upper bounds,
every independent pair of GF16 multiplication output combinations has MC=6.
This justifies a global constraint that five gates cannot already linearly
decode two independent target combinations, even if the five gates themselves
are nonlinear.

It does NOT justify replacing a useful nonlinear six-gate prefix by a quadratic
one when searching for an eight-gate full multiplier: an alternative optimal
pair circuit may lose auxiliary signals required by a cheap extension. It also
does not transfer three- or four-output quadratic lower bounds to unrestricted
circuits. A generic-pair lower bound of seven is false.

The primary 1990 Mirwald conference abstract additionally describes matrix-pair
rank via Kronecker invariants and reports a maximum of ceil(3n/2) for square
binary matrix pairs. This is corroborating context, not a dependency of the
explicit six-AND witnesses or the local lower-bound proof. Its exceptional
blocks were not classified or used here.

## Useful matrix-pencil synthesis family

For output trace coefficients a,b, the matrix pair is (M_a,M_b). After an
invertible change on one input it becomes (I,M_a^{-1}M_b); the latter operator
is multiplication by r=b/a. For the special class its characteristic polynomial
is (z^2+z+1)^2; for the generic class it is an irreducible quartic. This does
not imply different gate counts.

For a bilinear six-AND realization, group the products by their decoder columns.
The three two-product groups have matrices X, Y, Z of rank exactly two, with
M_a=X+Y and M_b=X+Z after naming the common group X. Thus bilinear six synthesis
can equivalently seek a matrix X with rank(X)=rank(X+M_a)=rank(X+M_b)=2 and
then factor the three matrices into two rank-one terms each. Necessity follows
from the decoder equality case and rank(M_a)=rank(M_b)=rank(M_a+M_b)=4;
sufficiency follows by those rank factorizations. The audit checks the three
rank-two groups for every supplied circuit.

For general parallel mixed-input quadratic gates, the analogous parameter uses
alternating polar matrices A with ranks(A)=ranks(A+F)=ranks(A+G)=4. Each rank-four
quadratic is a sum of two affine-input products modulo affine terms. This
parameterizes parallel six-AND pair circuits, not all unrestricted six-gate
prefixes. Neither family is imposed as a global search constraint here.

## Selector-space high-degree budget for any eight-gate candidate

Let g1,...,g8 be gate truth functions in topological order. Padding a smaller
circuit with affine or zero gates is allowed. Let E_i be the first i coordinate
subspace of F2^8. Define H:F2^8 -> (Boolean ANF terms of degree at least three)
by H(c)=high(sum c_j g_j), and write r_i=rank(H restricted to E_i).

Choose the actual four output-decoder rows; their span D has dimension four
because the four target classes are independent modulo affine functions.
Every element of D lies in ker H. Set s_i=dim(D intersection E_i) and
K_i=ker(H restricted to E_i). Then D intersection K_i=D intersection E_i, so

    8-r_8 >= dim(D+K_i) = 4+i-r_i-s_i,
    hence r_8-r_i <= 4-i+s_i.

This argument is in selector space and does not require independent gate
functions modulo affine terms or a minimal circuit. Constants and other
affine terms disappear from H and cannot cancel a rank-eight target.

Every nonzero target scalar has MC=4 (rank-eight scalar quadratic theorem).
Therefore s_1=s_3=0. Since the first AND has affine operands, r_1=0. The
following independent-of-pair-theorem conditions follow:

* r_8<=3.
* r_8-r_3<=1.

The published unrestricted pair lower bound of six implies s_5<=1. Consequently
r_8-r_5<=0; monotonicity gives r_8=r_5. This is the stronger condition that
all high-degree directions occur within the first five gates. Its published
two-output-theorem dependency must remain explicit. If r_8=3, the first three
gates already have high-degree rank two, so g2 and g3 supply independent
high-degree parts.

## Escape timing without and with the pair theorem

Suppose the first six gates are all quadratic, and let P6 be their truth span
together with all affine functions A. Because only two gates remain and the
target space T has dimension four modulo A, dim((P6 intersection (A+T))/A)>=2.
It cannot be at least three: six quadratic gates can be flattened, but a
three-output decoder has seven nonzero words of weight at least four, whereas
their total weight is at most 4*6=24<28. Thus the intersection is exactly two.

The missing target quotient (P6+T)/P6 has dimension two. Two remaining gate
directions must span it exactly. Hence both remaining gates belong to P6+T,
which is quadratic, and the entire circuit has only quadratic gate functions.
That contradicts the separately certified eight-gate quadratic exclusion.
This proves a necessary high-degree gate within the first six without invoking
the unrestricted two-output theorem. No prefix gate independence is required.

With the theorem-dependent equality r_8=r_5 and the same certified quadratic
exclusion (r_8>0), a high-degree gate must occur within the first five.

## Limits

No solver was run, no new full multiplier or AES circuit was obtained, no
performance improvement was measured, and no unrestricted eight-AND exclusion
or novelty claim is made. The parent is independently checking abstract rank
budget controls before changing search constraints. This run changes no search
encoder or tracked repository file.
